cards.text: Jesus has just finished praying to the Father for His disciples. Now He goes out with them across the Kidron Valley, and they enter a garden. Friend, grab your apron and hold on, because this is where the story turns.
There's just one problem with this garden. Judas, His betrayer, knows the place too.

cards.question: Why does Judas, the one betraying Jesus, know this garden?

answers.text: Jesus had often met there with His disciples
The chief priests had shown him the way there
His family had once owned the land nearby

cards.text: So Judas shows up, and he does NOT come alone. He brings a band of soldiers, plus officers.

cards.question: Judas brings officers along with the soldiers. Who are the officers from?
Judas and the crowd arrive at the garden carrying lanterns, torches and ___.

cards.text: Lanterns, torches, weapons, and more light than I saw in all my years in the back of that junk drawer. And Jesus? He knows all that is coming upon Him.

cards.question: The crowd is coming into the garden, and Jesus knows all that is coming upon Him. What does He do?

answers.text: Steps forward and asks who they are looking for
Slips back across the Kidron Valley in the dark
Hides deeper in the garden with His disciples

cards.question: The crowd tells Jesus they are looking for Jesus of Nazareth. True or false: Jesus tells them they have the wrong man.

cards.text: Jesus says, “I am He.” And Judas, His betrayer, is standing right there with the crowd.

cards.question: True or false: When Jesus tells the crowd “I am He,” they draw back and fall to the ground.

cards.text: Picture it, friend. The soldiers are picking themselves up off the ground, torches and all, and Jesus asks AGAIN, “Whom are you seeking?”

cards.question: The crowd gives the same answer: Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus says He already told them He is the one. Then what does He ask about His disciples?

answers.text: That the crowd let them go
That the crowd take them too
That the crowd question them first

cards.question: John says Jesus speaking up for His disciples fulfills a word He had spoken before. What was it?

answers.text: I have not lost one of those You have given Me
I will lead every one of you safely home tonight
The world will never lay a hand on any of you

cards.text: Then Simon Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, draws his sword. He strikes the servant of the high priest and cuts off his right ear.
The servant's name was Malchus. Friend, I bet losing an ear was NOT on his to-do list when he walked into that garden.

cards.question: True or false: After Peter cuts off Malchus's ear, Jesus tells Peter to keep his sword out and stand his ground.
Jesus tells Peter to put his sword away. Then He asks, “Shall I not drink the cup the ___ has given Me?”

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Trust me, friend, this story is FAR from over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 18 quotes "Shall I not drink the cup the ___ has given Me?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus has just finished praying to the Father for His disciples. That fact comes from John 17, but the card cites only John 18:1 and gives no reference for it. Verse 1 says only "After Jesus had spoken these words."

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only answer that sounds like Scripture ("those You have given Me") and the only one spoken to God rather than to the disciples. "I will lead every one of you safely home tonight" sounds modern next to it. A baker can pick the right answer by its style alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The to-do-list joke gets its laugh from Malchus losing his ear. It laughs at his injury rather than looking at his situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The humor across the walkthrough is mild: an apron line, one drawer comparison and a to-do-list line. None of it reaches laugh-out-loud, and several cards that could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact have none. Examples are Judas showing up with an army (card 4) and the crowd falling to the ground (card 12).

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend.

findings.problem: Card 19 is only the story-isn't-over line, which the docs allow. It tells no verse but cites John 18:11.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?
